source_notes: Skyrim Special Edition (Steam) publishes only a 'public' branch, so PICS only ever exposes the CURRENT manifest. Historical manifests below were recovered from community downgrade guides -- SKSE and most native-code mods break on every executable update, so the modding community has documented exact depot/manifest triples for every notable version since the Anniversary Edition (AE) launched in Nov 2021. Depot 489831 = main game content ('MAIN2' in some guides), 489832 = a second content depot ('MAIN'), 489833 = the executable ('EXE'). A fourth depot, 489838, carries optional Russian localization and was not recorded here (out of scope). Two classes of source were used: (1) individually-authored Steam Community guides, each verified by direct WebFetch of the guide page, and (2) the Nexus Mods article 'Steam Manifest List for Skyrim' (nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/articles/6536), a maintained table the author says is sourced from steamdb.info manifest histories -- fetched here via a Wayback Machine snapshot (web.archive.org, capture 2025-07-31) because Nexus Mods 403s direct curl/WebFetch from this environment. Confidence 'high' below means the Nexus article's numbers were independently corroborated by at least one separately-authored Steam Community guide with no shared authorship; 'low' means the Nexus article is the only source found (searches turned up no second independent source, including checks of the Nexus 'Unofficial Downgrade Patcher' mod page comments, r/skyrimmods, and Nexus/STEP forum threads, none of which quoted the raw manifest IDs). No conflicts were found between sources for any version recorded here -- all agreeing sources matched exactly. CORRECTION APPLIED: this run originally discarded the entire 1.6.342 entry because its depot-489831 manifest ('349141704917442044') is 18 digits and the initial brief said manifest GIDs must be 19-20 digits. That digit-count rule was wrong -- a manifest GID is any decimal value that fits a uint64 (1-20 digits), and 18-digit values occur legitimately roughly 1 time in 20. After the coordinator corrected the rule, 1.6.342 was restored below (still confidence 'low', single-sourced, unaffected in substance by the correction). This was the only manifest ID affected by the bad rule in this run -- no other candidate was discarded for being too short. Release dates are taken from the same Nexus article and are single-sourced (not independently cross-checked); build IDs were not obtainable without steamdb.info, which this task explicitly excludes, so 'build' is null throughout.
